title: Boss: the cipher lab
summary: Spot ECB in the wild, seek inside a CTR stream, catch a reused nonce, and seal database fields bound to their rows.

steps.title: The lab
body: Four jobs that combine the module: recognising ECB from ciphertext alone, using CTR's random access, exploiting a nonce reuse found during an audit, and building the AES-GCM field encryption you would actually ship.
Keys and nonces are fixed or counter-based so the tests are repeatable. In production the key comes from a vault and the nonce counter is persisted.

steps.title: ECB scanner
prompt: An audit dumped ciphertexts from several services, one hex string per line on standard input. For each line, print:
<line number>: ECB (<n> repeated blocks)      if any 16-byte block repeats an earlier one in that line
Line numbers start at 1. Count repeats as in lesson 2 (three equal blocks are 2 repeats). Ignore empty lines (they do not get a number).
steps.starter: // Read lines with Console.ReadLine() until it returns null.

tests.name: three equal blocks, blank line skipped

hints: `Convert.FromHexString(line)`, then step through 16 bytes at a time.
Keep a separate `HashSet<string>` for each line.

steps.title: Seek inside a CTR stream
prompt: CTR lets you decrypt from the middle of a large file without touching the start. Write `byte[] CtrAt(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] data, long offset)` that XORs `data` with the keystream **starting at byte `offset`** of the stream.
Use the same counter block as lesson 3: 8-byte nonce, then the block number as an 8-byte big-endian value. Byte `offset` lives in block `offset / 16`, at position `offset % 16` inside it.
The tests decrypt slices of a 100-byte stream at various offsets and compare with decrypting the whole thing.
starter: byte[] CtrAt(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] data, long offset)
solution: byte[] CtrAt(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] data, long offset)
template: Dojo.Eq("offset 0, first block uses AES(nonce || 0)", Convert.ToHexStringLower(dojoPlain.Take(16).Zip(dojoKs0, (a, b) => (byte)(a ^ b)).ToArray()), Convert.ToHexStringLower(dojoCipher[..16]));
Dojo.Eq("the whole stream decrypts", System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetString(dojoPlain), System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetString(CtrAt(dojoKey, dojoNonce, dojoCipher, 0)));
Dojo.Eq($"{dojoLen} bytes at offset {dojoOff}", System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetString(dojoPlain, dojoOff, dojoLen),
hints: For each output byte, its stream position is `offset + i`; its block is `position / 16`.
Only re-encrypt the counter block when the block number changes, and index the keystream with `position % 16`.

steps.title: Find the reused nonce
prompt: Three AES-GCM boxes (format: **nonce (12) || ciphertext || tag (16)**) came out of an audit, hex in the starter. You sent box 1 yourself, so you know its plaintext.

Print which two boxes share a nonce, as `boxes A and B share a nonce` (A < B, numbered from 1), then the plaintext of the **other** box in that pair, recovered without the key (it is no longer than box 1's message).
starter: string known = "Quarterly numbers are attached.";   // the plaintext of box 1
solution: string known = "Quarterly numbers are attached.";   // the plaintext of box 1
for (int b = a + 1; b < raw.Length; b++)
hints: Compare the first 12 bytes of each pair of boxes.
The ciphertext of a box is `raw[12..^16]`; XOR the two ciphertexts and the known plaintext, for the shorter length.

steps.title: Field encryption bound to its row
prompt: Build the field encryption for a `users` table. There is one data key (`key`, given) and a nonce counter `counter` (given, starts at 0):

- `byte[] SealField(int userId, string column, string value)`: take the next nonce (increment `counter`, then 4 zero bytes + `counter` as 8-byte big-endian, so the first is `...0001`), encrypt the UTF-8 value with AES-GCM (16-byte tag) with associated data `$"users:{userId}:{column}"` in UTF-8, and return **nonce || ciphertext || tag**.
- `string OpenField(int userId, string column, byte[] box)`: decrypt with the associated data rebuilt from the arguments.
The tests check exact bytes, that each seal uses a new nonce, and that a value copied to another user or another column refuses to decrypt.
starter: byte[] key = Enumerable.Range(0, 32).Select(i => (byte)(i * 5)).ToArray();   // in production: from a key vault
byte[] SealField(int userId, string column, string value)
string OpenField(int userId, string column, byte[] box)
solution: byte[] key = Enumerable.Range(0, 32).Select(i => (byte)(i * 5)).ToArray();   // in production: from a key vault
byte[] SealField(int userId, string column, string value)
using var gcm = new AesGcm(key, tagSizeInBytes: 16);
gcm.Encrypt(nonce, plain, box.AsSpan(12, plain.Length), box.AsSpan(12 + plain.Length), aad);
string OpenField(int userId, string column, byte[] box)
using var gcm = new AesGcm(key, tagSizeInBytes: 16);
gcm.Decrypt(box.AsSpan(0, 12), box.AsSpan(12, plain.Length), box.AsSpan(box.Length - 16), plain, aad);
template: Dojo.Eq("the first box uses nonce 1", "000000000000000000000001", Convert.ToHexStringLower(dojoBox[..12]));
var dojoEc = new byte[15]; var dojoEt = new byte[16];
Dojo.Eq("ciphertext and tag match AES-GCM with AAD users:42:email", Convert.ToHexStringLower(dojoEc) + Convert.ToHexStringLower(dojoEt), Convert.ToHexStringLower(dojoBox[12..]));
Dojo.Eq("OpenField reads it back", "ada@example.com", OpenField(42, "email", dojoBox));
Dojo.Check("sealing the same value twice gives different boxes", !dojoBox.SequenceEqual(dojoBox2), "two boxes were identical");
Dojo.Throws<System.Security.Cryptography.AuthenticationTagMismatchException>("copied to user 43, it refuses to open", () => OpenField(43, "email", dojoBox));
Dojo.Throws<System.Security.Cryptography.AuthenticationTagMismatchException>("moved to another column, it refuses to open", () => OpenField(42, "phone", dojoBox));
Dojo.Throws<System.Security.Cryptography.AuthenticationTagMismatchException>("a tampered box refuses to open", () => OpenField(42, "email", dojoBad));
hints: Build the same AAD string in both methods: `$"users:{userId}:{column}"`.
